newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to reduce red tape for investors-Dep PM.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to reduce red tape for investors-Dep PM.

text.p: Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Pynzenyk promised on Thursday to reduce the country's red-tape, blamed for hindering foreign investment.
"We are ready to cancel all unnecessary and artificially-created obstacles," he told a news conference.

He said measures include revising procedures to reduce the number of licenses required to run a business, elimination of permits granting the right to invest in Ukraine, partial deregulation of banking procedures and simplification of customs procedures.
Government officials have already promised to implement the changes next year.
Many foreign investors have loudly complained about the number of permits and licenses required when trying to do business in Ukraine.
About 100 permits are required to purchase a single piece of property.
Ukraine has attracted only $1.5 billion in foreign investment since winning independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.
